name: Defend With Purpose
display_title: Give your defense a next step
description: Turn frames and grip fights into progress toward an escape. Learn to choose a reachable next position, protect it, and recognize when stopping is the right response.
summary: Useful defense addresses the immediate threat and gives you a reachable next step toward more space, a guard, or a reversal.
overview: Sometimes the next step is small: free an elbow, turn onto a side, or stop a hand reaching your neck. Surviving while you rebuild those options is progress; you do not need to force a complete escape in one movement.
key_takeaways: Address a submission threat before attempting a positional escape; tap when you cannot defend safely.
Choose a nearby improvement you can describe, such as getting your elbow inside or recovering half guard.
Use the space a frame creates. If you never move into it, the top player has time to change the pin.
Keep the improvement you have earned before reaching for the next one.
An escape can be partial. Half guard with working frames may be a useful result from mount.

bjj_applications.scenario: You are under side control with your near elbow outside
bjj_applications.application: First make room to bring the elbow inside without extending both arms. Once you have a usable frame, move your hips and try to insert a knee.
bjj_applications.outcome: The first success is an inside frame; guard recovery is the next job.

bjj_applications.scenario: You are mounted and the top player follows every hip escape
bjj_applications.application: Protect your neck and keep your elbows near your body. Use a controlled bridge to make them adjust their base, then work your elbow and knee toward recovering a leg.
bjj_applications.outcome: You connect the bridge to a specific recovery instead of repeating a movement with no destination.

bjj_applications.scenario: You have recovered half guard but are still flat underneath
bjj_applications.application: Keep the trapped leg while rebuilding a frame and room to turn toward the opponent. Do not release the leg just to chase closed guard that is not yet available.
bjj_applications.outcome: You retain the progress of the escape while improving a still-difficult position.

common_mistakes.mistake: Trying to escape through an already secured submission
common_mistakes.consequence: The positional movement may tighten the finish or remove your remaining defense.
common_mistakes.correction: Defend the actual submission first and tap before injury; restart to practice an earlier decision.

common_mistakes.mistake: Rejecting any result short of full guard or top position
common_mistakes.consequence: You discard useful intermediate control and return to the pin.
common_mistakes.correction: Choose and secure one attainable improvement at a time.

training_exercises.name: One useful improvement
training_exercises.description: Start under side control with no submission applied. Bottom chooses a small goal, such as an inside elbow or a knee between the bodies; top holds the pin with agreed resistance. Reset on that improvement, a position change, or a tap.

training_exercises.name: Escape in two parts
training_exercises.description: Start under mount. Bottom first tries to recover half guard, then works from there toward an open guard; top tries to re-establish mount or pass. Reset after the second recovery, a settled pin, or a tap.
training_exercises.focus: Connect an escape to the work required in its landing position.

knowledge_assessment.question: Is holding a defensive position always passive?
knowledge_assessment.answer: No. Preventing a submission and rebuilding an inside frame can be the necessary work before any escape is available.

knowledge_assessment.question: You escaped mount to half guard. Is the escape wasted?
knowledge_assessment.answer: No. You recovered a leg barrier; now preserve it and improve your posture and frames.
